item.title: Correlations carried and controlled by coupled non-Markovian environments
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Extends the hierarchy of pure states (HOPS) to communicating non-Markovian environments with photon hopping, establishing that continuous monitoring and local feedback on interior cavities generate and enhance entanglement and correlations between unactuated endpoint spins.

Grade 0.445 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Stuart Flannigan

Figure

Homodyne measurement of the central cavity and feedback driving only the central spin increases endpoint spin-spin correlations (zz and yy) and endpoint concurrence over time across a three-cavity chain.

Asks

How can quantum systems coupled to spatially communicating, non-Markovian environments be simulated and controlled using local hierarchy methods?

But

Numerical truncation of hierarchy depth KH, Gaussian non-Markovian bosonic environments, zero-temperature initial bath vacuum.

Tools

Correlated hierarchy of pure states (HOPS) · Non-Markovian quantum state diffusion · Continuous homodyne measurement and feedback · Matrix product states (MPS)

Code. https://github.com/SFlann/correlated-hops

Abstract

An environment can retain quantum information and carry it between spatially separated systems. Describing the combined influence of these processes requires a treatment of both environmental memory and spatial correlations. Here, we formulate a local hierarchy of pure states for quantum systems coupled to spatially correlated, non-Markovian environments whose modes themselves exchange excitations. We use this method to describe the reduced spin dynamics of a chain of locally coupled Rabi spin--cavity pairs motivated by cavity-QED implementations, where photon hopping in the eliminated cavity environment generates correlations and entanglement between otherwise isolated spins. Monitoring intermediate cavities and feeding their measurement records back onto the corresponding spins further enhances correlations between endpoint spins that receive no direct feedback. The delayed response when feedback starts, and continued entanglement growth after it stops, support a mechanism in which coherent environmental dynamics carry the effects of earlier feedback to the endpoint spins. Finally, tensor-network simulations of XXZ and Heisenberg chains show how environmental transport changes many-body correlation patterns. These results show how coupled environments and local feedback can control correlations between distant spins. We provide a numerically exact stochastic pure-state framework for simulating these processes, opening up avenues to explore the coherent and dissipative control of interacting non-Markovian many-body systems.

item.title: Packet-wise multi-hop quantum routing of hybrid quantum-classical packets
item.description:
Worth a look new method — Demonstrated double-hop routing of hybrid quantum-classical packets across two cascaded routers to three receivers without regenerating classical headers. Delivered time-bin BB84 QKD payloads with non-zero secret key rates.

Grade 0.444 · 1.7σ above the day's baseline · matched “Cavity-based quantum networks with single atoms and optical photons” · Tae Yeong Park, Youn Chang Jeong, Myeong Soo Kang, Kwang Yong Song, Paul G. Kwiat, Hee Su Park

Asks

Can quantum routers dynamically deliver hybrid quantum-classical packets over multi-hop paths without disturbing payloads or regenerating classical headers at intermediate nodes?

Before

Prior quantum routers required splitting classical and quantum components with wavelength splitters, switching, and regenerating classical headers before transmission.

But

Demonstrated for two cascaded hops and three terminal receivers.

Tools

optical-fiber-based quantum router · hybrid quantum-classical packets · time-bin qubits · two-decoy-state BB84 protocol

Abstract

The ability to dynamically route quantum information across multiple nodes is a key requirement for realizing versatile and scalable quantum networks. Quantum routers are devices to achieve packet-level routing beyond static point-to-point connections by handling hybrid packets combining classical headers and quantum payloads. Previously proposed methods have selectively accessed the classical and quantum components of the packets utilizing wavelength splitters and optical switches, and repacked the hybrid packets before transmission through the outgoing link with regenerating classical headers. This work reports a novel optical-fiber-based quantum router that minimizes the disturbance and latency on the hybrid packets through more transparent operation. We experimentally demonstrate double-hop routing via two cascaded routers to three distinct receivers without regeneration of the headers. As a practical application, quantum key distribution packets based on time-bin qubits and a BB84 protocol with a two-decoy-state method are successfully delivered to the three receivers achieving nonzero secret key rates. These results demonstrate the feasibility of extensive quantum networks interconnected by multiple-step router nodes.

item.title: Observation of strong electric dipole-dipole interactions between two atoms
item.description:
Worth a look new result — Atom pairs confined to 20 nm spatial width reach densities n>1016/cm3 (nk−3>10), producing near-field electric dipole-dipole interactions where coherent forces exceed the dissipative rate and a single emitted photon imparts momentum transfers up to ∼10ℏk (median 7.8ℏk).

Grade 0.437 · 1.6σ above the day's baseline · matched “Quantum information with Rydberg atoms” · Yu-Kun Lu, Jiahao Lyu, Wolfgang Ketterle

Figure

Time-of-flight momentum distributions of atom pairs following decay from the excited state at different wavepacket RMS sizes (22 nm, 35 nm, and 93 nm), showing broad non-Gaussian momentum components with median values reaching 7.8ℏk due to near-field dipolar acceleration.

Asks

How do two neutral atoms interact with light when placed at sub-optical-wavelength distances where near-field electric dipole-dipole interactions exceed spontaneous emission?

Before

Cold atom dipolar studies were limited to far-field mean-field or collective regimes with nk−3≲1.

But

Measurements isolate two-body doublon physics via subtraction of singlon background; photoassociation loss rates deviate from static models due to dynamical phase-space depletion of the Franck-Condon region.

Tools

3D optical lattice · Bose-Einstein condensate of ¹⁶²Dy · Mott insulator doublons · Time-of-flight absorption imaging

Abstract

We have prepared pairs of atoms at densities exceeding 10¹⁶/cm³ corresponding to nlambdabar³>10 and studied how they interact with light. In this regime, the coherent part of the electric dipole-dipole interaction is larger than the dissipative part, and a single photon emission can transfer large momenta (larger than ten times the single photon recoil) to the atoms. For off-resonant laser light, the atoms are dressed with an electric dipole moment of ≈ 1 Debye and interact coherently. This light-induced dipole-dipole interaction has been previously observed only in the far-field mean-field regime. For two atoms, the resonance is shifted by the two-body Lamb shift which is dominated by the near-field part of the dipolar interaction. Dipolar resonance shifts have been observed before only for many atoms interacting with the far-field part of the dipolar interaction. Our work sheds new light on photoassociation processes and paves the way for studying driven quantum systems with strong electric dipole-dipole interactions.
